tests.input: How do Moltbot's persistent memory and multi-channel integration work together to change how users interact with it?
tests.actual_output:
In combination they turn Moltbot from a one-off chat responder into a continuous, cross-device collaborator.

How they work together (summary)
- Persistent local memory (plain Markdown/JSON on the user’s filesystem) saves conversation history, user preferences, ongoing project state, custom instructions, file locations and configs so context survives across days/weeks.
- Multi-channel integration (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage, Teams, Matrix, WebChat, native apps, etc.) lets users access that same, persistent agent state from any device or interface they already use.

What that enables for users
- Stateful continuity: start a task on one channel/device and continue later on another without re-explaining context (e.g., begin a website on desktop and finish via Telegram on your phone).
- Personalization that persists: Moltbot remembers working patterns, custom instructions and project state so responses and actions are increasingly tailored over time.
- Real automation across channels: because Moltbot can execute actions (browser automation via a managed Chromium/CDP, cron jobs, mailbox reorganization, API calls, etc.), users get end-to-end task execution rather than just suggestions — invoked from any channel.
- Proactive, timely help: with saved context and multi-channel reach it can send reminders, heartbeats, daily briefings, monitor systems and push alerts wherever you are.
- Extensible capabilities everywhere: community skills (ClawdHub) become usable from any connected channel, so new automations are immediately available across devices.

Practical result
- The interaction model shifts from “ask a question, get an isolated answer” to “engage an ongoing assistant that knows your projects, preferences and history and can act proactively or when asked, from any interface.”

Caveat (security/attack surface)
- Because memory and credentials are stored locally (often plaintext) and Moltbot accepts input over many messaging channels, this combined design also widens attack surfaces (prompt injection, credential exposure, backdoor risk) — something to mitigate with secure storage and channel filtering.
